articles.headline: 'We f**ked up': 1 day into Wardogs Season 2, the Blue team bribery bonus is being dropped
keyFacts: Bulkhead Interactive removed the Blue team XP and cash bribery bonus one day into Wardogs Season 2 because top-tier players used it to dominate matches.
CEO Joe Brammer admitted the studio made a mistake with the bonus, which also negatively impacted how players joined and started games.
Bulkhead is also fixing driver progression issues and issuing 24-hour bans and wipes to less than 1,000 players exploiting fast tank access.
body: One day into Wardogs Season 2, Bulkhead Interactive has decided to scrap the bribery plan it announced last week as a way to help convince players to join the Blue team. The problem isn't that the plan didn't work—it actually worked far too well.
THE PLAN:
- "Lonestar cash and XP bonus. Season 2 only. New Bakurani spawn."
- "We're looking at how we can help the win rate of a certain team." -Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer (via "Road to Season 2" devlog)
THE REALITY:
- "We were wrong. We fucked up," Brammer admitted in a new video (via RPS).
- Blue team is now winning "by far, the most," Brammer said, even though the actual boosts are not terribly substantial: 5% Lonestar cash and 2.5% XP.
- "Median" players didn't get much from those percentages, but Bulkhead found that "top tier" players were seeing significant boosts
- Bottom line: it's gone.

"We're removing the Blue XP bonus, the cash bonus. We were wrong," Brammer said. Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott added that the studio thought Blue team bonus might work out this way, but said "I don't think we expected it to be this much of a swing."

I can't say I'm terribly surprised by the outcome. I'm not a Wardogs player, but I have been around long enough to know how these things go: If you dangle a competitive edge in front of gamers, they're going to jump for it. Percentage boosts are especially risky because they're performance-based and so much more likely to go spinning out of control, especially in the hands of, as Brammer put it, "tryhards."

And it's not just the extra XP and cash being earned that's a problem: Philpott said the bonus is also "impacting people joining games and starting games," presumably because if they can't be a Blue, they'll leave and try their luck with another game.

(Quick side note: I'm not a fan of the term 'tryhard.' Of course I'm trying hard! Why wouldn't I be? My nephew called me a tryhard once and I told him that maybe if he tried harder he wouldn't get his ass kicked so hard. He was 12 and I got some disapproving looks from other people at the Christmas party, but I stand by it.)

PC Gamer's Morgan Park, who is a Wardogs guy, also made the call when this plan was unveiled last week: "XP and cash bribes are a drastic move, but should have a real impact. It's unclear how big these boosts will be, but I expect Blue will instantly become the most popular team by a wide margin in Season 2."

Predictable as this outcome was, I don't see it as a particularly egregious misstep. Brammer called it an "experiment," and sometimes that's what you have to do—and the early stages of a massively popular videogame with teething issues can definitely be one of those times. Brammer also noted that other changes aimed at rebalancing things, including new spawns on the Bakurani map, have proven effective and will remain.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Alongside the removal of the Blue team bribery, Bulkhead is also fixing issues with driver progression, and is fixing a driver exploit that's letting players access tanks too quickly: Players who are "very clearly" taking advantage of the exploit (less than 1,000 in total, according to Brammer) will be given a 24-hour ban from the game and have their cash and XP wiped.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

articles.headline: Why Texans fans should temper expectations for Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Week 6 debut
keyFacts: The Houston Texans officially traded for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. following their Week 5 win over the Tennessee Titans.
Coach DeMeco Ryans stated that Harrison will play in his team debut during Week 6 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.
Reporter BJ Dien-Aime indicated that fans should temper expectations because Harrison will play in a limited role.
body: Following the Houston Texans' Week 5 win over the Tennessee Titans, the Texans made their trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. official. It appeared he was headed to Houston before they played, but the Texans wanted to win before officially making the deal.

Now that they won and are 1-4 on the year, they face the Jacksonville Jaguars in London with a chance to build some significant momentum to make an incredible comeback and make the playoffs. Plus, Texans fans will get to see Harrison suit up this weekend.

However, according to a report from ESPN's BJ Dien-Aime, Texans fans should temper their expectations of what Harrison will do this weekend in his Texans debut. He'll play, but it's going to be in a limited role.
Texans fans should temper expectations for Marvin Harrison Jr. in team debut
"New WR Marvin Harrison Jr. is playing, according to coach DeMeco Ryans," Bien-Aime writes. "... Don't expect Harrison to play most of the offensive snaps, but there will be packages for him."
Texans fans will see Harrison suit up for their favorite team in Week 6 in the team's London matchup against the AFC South-leading Jaguars.
But his involvement in the offense is not expected to be on par with Nico Collins or any of the other main pieces of this offense.

It would not be a surprise, based on the fact that the Texans aren't going to heavily feature Harrison, if Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel, and even Kayshon Boutte saw more playing time in Week 6 than Harrison.

The new Texans' WR is going to see the field, and he probably will get a few targets with plays designed for him. But this is his first week with his new team. It would not be a surprise if his involvement was limited.
If Harrison plays less than 50% of the snaps in Week 6, Texans fans shouldn't panic, as there is good reason why they will slow play Harrison.
Of course, it's possible that the Texans trust Harrison and C.J. Stroud's connection to thrive right away, and he's out there more than expected.

But Texans fans should temper expectations for Harrison's debut with the team this Sunday. He'll play and get some opportunities, but it likely won't be the full complement of plays for Harrison in Week 6.

articles.headline: How Jaedyn Shaw is holding Gotham's attack together during NWSL Shield pursuit
keyFacts: Gotham FC prepares to play the Washington Spirit on Saturday while pursuing the NWSL Shield with three regular season games remaining.
Gotham FC head coach Juan Carlos Amoros said fans must wait and see if Jaedyn Shaw will play following a minor injury.
Gotham FC has conceded the fewest goals in the league, but several top scorers are currently underperforming their expected goals.
body: Is Jaedyn Shaw the one thing keeping Gotham FC's season together? While this may feel like a strange question to pose, for a team that's en route to winning the NWSL Shield for the most points in the regular season, Gotham's stats have been quite odd. As Gotham prepare to travel to face the Washington Spirit on Saturday, it's worth taking a look at those Shield credentials with three games left in the regular season.

Unfortunately, there's a chance that we could get an answer to this question during the match. Shaw left United States U-23 international duty with a minor injury and is considered day-to-day at this stage. When asked about her availability for this top-of-the-table clash, Gotham FC head coach Juan Carlos Amoros simply said, "Wait and see."

Gotham have conceded the fewest goals in the league while also scoring the 12th-most goals of any team. They have the second-best goal difference due to their defensive play, but when looking deeper at the numbers, they aren't clearly the best team in the league; that's likely the San Diego Wave. By the numbers, the team chasing them has the better goal difference and expected goals difference.

Of course, soccer is played on grass and not spreadsheets, but this is important to take note of, with the playoffs around the corner. That xG underperformance on the attacking side of the ball is something that could come back to bite this team, as of the top five scorers this season, four are significantly underperforming their xG. Ester Gonzalez may no longer be with the team, but she was close to hitting her expected numbers with six goals from an xG of 7.85. Sam Kerr has four goals from 9.58 xG, Rose Lavelle has four from 6.26 xG, Jordynn Dudley has four from 5.76 xG, and then there's Shaw.
How to watch Washington Spirit vs. Gotham FC, odds
Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time: 12:30 p.m. ET
Location: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.
TV: CBS
Odds: Washington Spirit +160; Draw +230; NJ/NJ Gotham +155

While it was surprising not to see Shaw in the most recent United States women's national team camp facing Spain, Emma Hayes made the point that she wanted Shaw to play consistent minutes with the U-23s rather than come off the bench, given the national team's depth on the wings. That's understandable, but Gotham need Shaw to continue performing at this level, or an attack that is already underperforming will crater on the season.

Luckily, there isn't a position that Shaw can't get a shot off from or an area of the pitch that she can't score from. Be it cutting inside from the wing, popping up with a header or just taking a rip from outside the box, she's got you covered. And with so many other stars on this Gotham team, other NWSL sides can't focus on taking away Shaw because then someone else will make them pay.

Despite the inefficiency in attack, the club's defense makes this a strong side, even if it's no longer the true super team Gotham were trying to build in New Jersey. That may even be for the best, as to win the NWSL championship, sides have to be well-rounded and have multiple avenues to create danger, which Gotham have.

That could be enough to win a championship, but if a team can limit Shaw's shots, there are fair questions about what Gotham will do next. Facing the third-placed Washington Spirit will be a good test in that regard, but they're more of a test of Gotham's defense than they are of Gotham's attack. But to win a championship, they'll likely need to go through the Spirit anyway, and with the final set for Audi Field, this is good preparation, making Saturday's clash must-watch TV.

articles.headline: Porsche’s electric Macan Turbo is an automotive existential crisis
keyFacts: A TechCrunch reviewer tested the electric Porsche Macan Turbo, a crossover featuring 630 horsepower and a 100-kilowatt-hour battery.
The electric Macan Turbo starts at $112,700, and the tested model cost $149,610 including options and destination fees.
The reviewer reported 285 miles of highway range and fast charging, but noted the vehicle's EV navigation system was underwhelming.
body: Maybe it was the grey color, the slightly bulbous roofline, or the vaguely SUV-like proportions of the electric Porsche Macan, but as I shuttled kids and groceries around city and suburban streets, I never once noticed a longing stare from other drivers. Unlike with other cars I’ve tested, no enthusiasts stopped to ask me questions.

The 2026 Porsche Macan Turbo simply blended in, leaving in its wake a raft of existential questions. What is a sports car, anyway? Does it need to be overwhelmingly extroverted? Should it match the leaner, lighter look of its gas-powered sibling?

Drive one and the questions cease. Maybe that’s because the acceleration makes it hard to breathe? Or maybe it’s because, by the numbers, the Macan is a sports car at heart despite its rather humdrum crossover body style.

My passengers would agree. The kids I drove to soccer practice, both my own and others, gave the punchy acceleration high marks. The G-forces it reports on the head-up display ($2,660) can easily mimic the pull of gravity. Stab the accelerator at 70 mph and it lurches as though it were standing still. (Don’t worry, fellow parents. I did not try that with children on board.)

On winding roads, the car comes alive, thanks in part to the four-wheel steering ($2,150). Drop it into Sport Plus mode, and the car literally drops on its air suspension. Are we sure this is another anonymous crossover? Maybe anonymity is a useful trait in a car this responsive and powerful.

Unlike most two-row crossovers, you get the feeling of sitting in the Macan, not on it. The wheel extends far enough to make a sporty driving position possible, and the classic Porsche chronometer ($1,040) perched atop the dash ticks off the seconds it takes to get the kid to soccer practice.
Nuts and bolts

The 2027 Porsche Macan Turbo EV is a two-row crossover with 630 horsepower and a 100-kilowatt-hour battery. The EV, which the automaker provided to me for a week, starts at $112,700. However, the one I drove rang up at $149,610, including destination fees. Yes, the options alone could buy a nicely equipped Chevy Bolt. With Porsche and options, if you have to ask…well, it’s better not to.

The Porsche Macan Turbo EV I drove came in Slate Grey Neo (a $2,620 upgrade), which was really well executed and among the best greys I’ve seen. If you crave luxurious anonymity, then this grey is your color.

There were a slew of other options, and in my view, not all of them are worth it. I’d skip the passenger display ($1,710); my kids liked that it could play YouTube videos, but they can’t ride up front, and my wife was underwhelmed. “Our washing machine can play YouTube videos,” she said.

I’d also forgo include an illuminated Porsche wordmark on the front seatbacks ($690), puddle lamps that shine “PORSCHE” onto the pavement ($420), Porsche crests on the headrests ($640), and an illuminated Turbo badge on the door sills ($1,230).

That Turbo badge became a point of contention for some of my friends, who were quick to point out that EVs technically can’t have turbos. That is true, though automotive names have long been divorced from reality. Almost every Porsche these days has a turbo, even those not labeled as such.

It’s not just Porsche: BMW’s model numbers, for example, stopped reflecting engine displacement decades ago, and the Ford Galaxie never traveled between star systems using its hyperdrive. Sorry, friends, I’m not taking the bait.

At least the Macan Turbo’s EV qualities don’t raise too many questions. It charges fast — exactly 20 minutes from 19% to 80% on a 350-kilowatt charger — and gets about 285 miles of highway range. Those big wheels ($4,110) and sticky tires ($660) sapped some range, but it was still more than enough to get from New York to Boston with charge to spare.

The advanced driver assistance system ($1,140) works well enough, even if it hunts a bit in the lane. The AI-powered voice assistant did a solid job of interpreting my queries and commands. For a while, I thought it was the only way to turn on the heated steering wheel ($720), which was actually fine because it worked so well. (Surprise! There’s a small button hidden on the inner rim of the steering wheel between two spokes. IYKYK, I guess.)

When it’s time to leave the Macan, you can just open the door and walk away. The Burmester sound system ($4,960) will keep bumpin’ until you lock the door, which is a helpful reminder. If you’re a Porsche traditionalist, you can also hit the vestigial power button to the left of the driver’s display. Good to have choices, I guess? At least Porsche doesn’t charge you for that.
Where it fell short
The navigation system, and specifically how it integrates with the EV, was underwhelming.

When the car was at a 22% state of charge, I asked it to find the nearest fast charger. It directed me to two. Not two different options, but two chargers that I was supposed to use sequentially. The first was a 50-kilowatt charger in a mall parking lot ten minutes away. There, I was supposed to add a few percentage points before unplugging and driving across the street to another mall’s parking lot, where I would finish at a 350-kilowatt charger.

Wait, what? I ignored the machine and drove straight to the 350-kilowatt charger, arriving at 19%. As backed into the stall, the car was still commanding me to drive to the slower charger. I guess it didn’t want the battery to dip below 20%? Too late. There’s probably a setting to change that somewhere, but it wasn’t obvious. At least the charge rate peaked at 245 kilowatts, close to the 270-kilowatt maximum.
The electric Macan is like the answer to an esoteric Jeopardy! question: What does an identity crisis look like in the automotive industry? I’ll take a Porsche Macan Turbo for $150,000, Alex.

For anyone with deep enough pockets, EVs have blurred the line between sports cars and everything else. True gear heads will have another car to race, but if you want to spend a few hours carving corners, the Macan will do just fine. As a bonus, you can also use it in real life and won’t pay through the nose to keep it filled up.
Actually, that raises another question, this one for my editor: Can I get a fatter paycheck?

articles.headline: Have a Meta business account? You’re consenting to AI scraping now, legal experts say
keyFacts: Meta's updated commercial terms allow web scrapers to crawl websites associated with business accounts, Nieman Lab reported.
News publishers are affected, and Nieman Lab reported Meta could avoid licensing deals for AI training data.
The changes take effect on October 30 without an opt-out, meaning publishers must accept web-scraping or leave the platform.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- Meta Business Suite’s new terms allow web-crawling on publication sites, legal experts say.
- The change goes into effect on Oct. 30.
- Meta says the updated terms are a “consolidation” of pre-existing conditions.
Meta’s new commercial terms allow its web scrapers, bots, and agents to crawl websites “associated with” Meta business accounts, including news publishers, according to a report by Nieman Lab.

The terms apply to accounts that use Meta Business Suite’s account dashboard. Companies manage their Instagram profiles, Facebook pages, Messenger, and WhatsApp channels through Meta Business Suite. ZDNET uses Meta Business Suite to analyze and schedule posts across social media platforms.
More from ZDNET
What’s changing

The changes go into effect on Oct. 30, and Meta will not provide an opt-out, meaning publishers will either agree to the web-scraping or be booted from the platform. These are Meta’s new terms and conditions for web-crawling:

You authorize us (or any entity acting on our behalf) to use automated software (such as web scrapers, bots, robots, spiders, crawlers, and user agents) and create test credentials to access, index, cache, analyze, collect, retrieve, or crawl the domains, web pages, or URLs (and any content available through them) that are associated with your products or services, or that are made available through your or users’ use of Meta Company Products and services, and to periodically pull updates from such domains, web pages, or URLs. Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of, the Meta Company Products, services, and features provided under these Commercial Terms and any other applicable supplemental terms.
Publishers vs. AI companies

Meta could be avoiding entering licensing deals with many websites and news publications through this new web-scraping language, Nieman Lab reports. Tech companies need tons of data and information to train their AI models, but not just any data will do. Journalistic content makes for a high-quality dataset because it’s traditionally been fact-checked and edited, which personal blogs or other text scraped from the open internet may not be.

But, in part because of how AI search features have negatively impacted traffic to news sites (and therefore ad dollars), publishers (including Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company) have launched copyright lawsuits against AI companies for using their content, both for model training and providing answers to search queries without attribution. Several AI labs have forged licensing agreements with news publications to avoid this.
Meta defended its position, saying that it is consolidating its commercial and self-serve ad terms, according to the Verge. Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.headline: The top five club sides in football history
keyFacts: Paris Saint-Germain recently defeated Manchester City four to two in a match at the Etihad stadium.
TalkSPORT co-host Darren Bent ranked five historic club sides, placing Luis Enrique's current PSG team at number five.
Darren Bent ranked Barcelona's 2014 to 2015 team featuring Messi, Neymar, and Suarez as the greatest club side of all time.
body: Paris Saint-Germain reasserted themselves as the best club side on the planet on Wednesday night.
Despite a shaky start to their domestic campaign in France, the back-to-back European champions returned to their electrifying best against Manchester City in a 4-2 victory at the Etihad.
PSG are out to win a third successive Champions League title this season AFP

Playing against the current Premier League leaders, who have won all six domestic matches so far this term, Luis Enrique’s side cut through them like butter and raced into a three-goal lead before half-time.
It would eventually become a more evenly matched affair, and City spurned a number of glorious opportunities that could have altered the result.

But the first half, particularly the first goal from Desire Doue, reminded the rest of Europe that PSG are unstoppable on their day – leaving commentators, pundits and fans blown away by their quality.
It got us thinking: where does this PSG team rank amongst the greatest club sides in history?
According to ex-England striker and talkSPORT co-host Darren Bent , they come in at number five…
5. Paris Saint-Germain — Luis Enrique rebuild era (2024–2026)
Manager : Luis Enrique
Trophies : 2x Ligue 1, 1x Coupe de France, 2x Champions League
Regular players : Gianluigi Donnarumna/Matvey Safonov, Achraf Hakimi, Marquinhos, Willian Pacho, Nuno Mendes, Fabian Ruiz, Vitinha, Joao Neves, Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia
Formation : 4-3-3
Luis Enrique finally ended PSG’s long wait for the Champions League – and the first time was so nice, they had to do it twice.
Their thumping of Inter Milan in 2025 was followed by a hard-fought victory over Mikel Arteta’s pragmatic Arsenal in a clash of styles that was eventually decided on penalties earlier this year.
What’s more, PSG taught the modern football world a lesson: 11 players working in perfect harmony is more effective than three superstars.
This success all came after the departures of Lionel Messi , Kylian Mbappe and Neymar .
Bent said: “I think the reason why I’ve got these at five is because, when you look at teams sometimes, I know a lot of people always look at individuals.
“But Luis Enrique got rid of the superstars, got rid of the superstars to make this team.”
Arsenal’s Gabriel missed the decisive spot-kick, but few would argue PSG were the best club side in Europe last season Getty
4. Man United – Ronaldo, Rooney, Tevez era (2007 to 2009)
Manager : Sir Alex Ferguson
Trophies : 3x Premier League, 1x Champions League, 1x League Cup, 1x Club World Cup, 2x Community Shield

Regular players : Edwin van der Sar, Wes Brown/Gary Neville, Nemanja Vidic, Rio Ferdinand, Patrice Evra, Cristiano Ronaldo, Paul Scholes, Michael Carrick, Ji-Sung Park/Ryan Giggs, Wayne Rooney, Carlos Tevez/Dimitar Berbatov
Formation : 4-4-2 or 4-3-3
Only one Premier League team makes the list, and it is not the Arsenal Invincibles, Jose Mourinho’s Chelsea , Manchester City’s Centurions and treble winners, or Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool .
It is Sir Alex Ferguson’s Manchester United team between 2007 and 2009 – which won three consecutive Premier League titles and the Champions League.
Besides the team accolades, Cristiano Ronaldo collected the first of five Ballon d’Ors during his time in this famous Red Devils side.
Bent, who played against this team, was pressed over whether they should feature over the treble winners of 1999 – to which he simply replied: “Ronaldo and Rooney were better than all of them.”
Man United broke Chelsea’s period of dominance in the Premier League between 2007 and 2009 Getty
3. Bayern Munich – total domination (2012/2013)
Manager : Jupp Heynckes
Trophies : 1x Champions League, 1x Bundesliga, 1x DFB-Pokal, 1x DFL-Supercup
Regular players : Manuel Neuer, Philipp Lahm, Jerome Boateng, Dante, David Alaba, Javi Martinez, Bastian Schweinsteiger, Arjen Robben, Thomas Müller, Franck Ribery, Mario Mandzukic
Formation : 4-2-3-1
This Bayern Munich side became the first (and only, alongside their 2019/20 team) German club to win the European Treble.

They broke a number of records in the process, including the most points in Bundesliga history (winning the league by a massive 25-point margin) and clinching the title with six games to spare (earliest in history).
Bent said: “They won everything. Every trophy they were up for that year, they won it.
“They won the Champions League and the three trophies in their division.
“They broke 22 records that season. And some of those records were most points and biggest lead over second.”
Bayern Munich beat arch-rivals Borussia Dortmund to win the Champions League at Wembley in 2013 AFP
2. Real Madrid – three-peat era (2015–2018)
Manager : Zinedine Zidane
Trophies : 3x Champions League, 1x La Liga, 2x UEFA Super Cup, 2x FIFA Club World Cup, 1x Supercopa de Espana
Regular players : Keylor Navas, Dani Carvajal, Raphael Varane, Sergio Ramos, Marcelo, Luka Modric, Casemiro, Toni Kroos, Gareth Bale/Isco, Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema
Formation : 4-3-1-2 or 4-3-3
Second on the list is the only team in modern history to win three consecutive Champions Leagues (2016, 2017, 2018).

With Ronaldo in his prime, this team scored in 73 consecutive official matches across all competitions between April 2016 and September 2017, tying Santos’ historic world record set with the help of Pele.
While they were often outperformed by Barcelona on a domestic level, Bent believes their unprecedented European dominance supersedes that.
“I don’t think they were too bothered about LaLiga,” he said. “It was all about the Champions League.”
Ronaldo was the crown jewel in this Real Madrid side, but had superstar talent such as Bale, Benzema and Modric around him Getty
1. Barcelona – the height of Messi, Neymar, Suarez (2014/15)
Manager : Luis Enrique
Trophies : 1x Champions League, 1x La Liga, 1x Copa del Rey

articles.headline: Castlevania‘s Most Iconic Song Should Chain Whip Me To Death, Not Put Me In A Thousand Year Sleep
keyFacts: The reviewer stated that the soundtrack for Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse features an eclectic downtempo collection that works well as background ambiance.
The reviewer highlighted specific tracks like 'Bone March' and 'Iron Clock' as particular favorites during gameplay.
The reviewer criticized the game's arrangement of the iconic theme song 'Bloody Tears' for lacking intensity and energy.
body: As I continue my way through Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse (now blessedly disentangled from the platforming challenge that hemmed me up earlier this week), I find myself really vibing with the game’s soundtrack. The sound team at Evil Empire chose to go with an eclectic downtempo collection of work that feels in tune with the current musical zeitgeist, obsessed with the Lofi Girl and her many musical siblings.

It’s a good fit that makes the game stand out sonically in much the same way that it does mechanically and visually while still feeling good to listen to. It’s not obnoxious in the way some soundtracks can be, where louder, busier songs can burrow into your brain and become mercilessly stuck, like the harpsichords blaring in the Long Library in Symphony of the Night. I could play the Belmont’s Curse soundtrack in the background during a work day and be quite relaxed with the resulting ambiance.

I’m particularly fond of “Bone March,” a track that plays during your exploration of the Paris Catacombs, and “Iron Clock,” the theme for the Clock Tower. And though the Talos boss fight itself gave me heartburn and some severe hand calluses, “Stone Tyrant,”Â his boss theme, is actually quite funky.

But there’s one significant exception to my general enjoyment of Belmont’s Curse soundtrack: The way it treats “Bloody Tears” is kinda tragic. That song is the iconic theme song across the franchise. It’s up there with Dr. Wily’s Castle Theme from Mega Man 2, the kinda shit that when you hear it, it makes you want to run through a brick wall. And previous “Bloody Tears” themes understood that particular assignment. Hell, even the “Bloody Tears” arrangement for the Castlevania Dead Cells DLC is a bop.

But in Belmont’s Curse, the song feels like a pulled punch. There’s a build-up with the familiar run of notes that lets you know, “Yeah, the good shit you remember is coming,” but when it’s time for the beat drop after all that intense buildup, the song fades into almost nothing. It’s too orchestral, lacking the edge that I’ve come to expect from my “Bloody Tears” arrangements. It blends into the background.
“Bloody Tears” should get you hype. It should match the energy required to fight and defeat Dracula. This version, sadly, puts me into a thousand years’ sleep.

articles.headline: Blanche hopes to replicate success of Memphis crime task force to other cities
keyFacts: Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that Memphis crime dropped 34 percent following the launch of a joint federal and local task force.
Blanche and Senator Marsha Blackburn attributed the drop to interagency cooperation, which Blanche hopes to replicate in cities like Chicago.
Blanche said that the Memphis Safe Task Force will continue its crime-fighting operations past its one-year mark.
body: Attorney General Todd Blanche celebrated on Friday the work of the joint federal and local operation cracking down on crime in Memphis just over a year ago, hoping to replicate efforts across the country with similar cooperation between different law enforcement agencies.

Law enforcement officials from the federal government and Memphis held a roundtable Friday in the city, just over a year after the Trump administration launched the Memphis Safe Task Force aimed at public safety efforts in the crime-ridden city. Blanche said that crime in the city has dropped to a 25-year low, noting that overall crime is down 34% compared to last year.

“What it actually means on a day-to-day basis is the citizens of this county, the citizens of Tennessee, are in a safer environment, in a safer street, in a safer restaurant, in a safer building than they were two years ago, and that’s true across the country,” Blanche said, also touting crime-fighting efforts outside the city.

“We’re here to talk about Memphis, but the historic drop in crime that we’ve seen in this city is something that we’ve seen all across the country, and it’s completely the result of the work of the men and women who wear the badge, and who are working hard to keep communities safe,” he added.

Blanche shared that murders are down 33% compared to last year, while sexual assaults are down 25%, motor vehicle thefts are down 54%, robberies are down are down 40%, and aggravated assaults are down 24%. Officials also highlighted the successful efforts locating and recovering 196 missing or endangered children and returning them to safety.

The attorney general emphasized the need for cooperation across all levels in fighting crime, arguing it could work in other cities, naming Chicago as an example where law enforcement could work on lowering crime levels.

“The reason why this works, and the reason why we’re here today, the reason why we want other cities to look at Memphis, is because of the fact that nobody standing alone can accomplish what we’ve been able to accomplish,” Blanche said. “If only some of us stood together, it would still fail.”
The DOJ has faced public opposition from several Democratic-run cities regarding crime fighting, particularly when it comes to immigration enforcement.
Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) highlighted that cooperation between law enforcement agencies has been the key to fighting crime in Memphis.
FEDERAL CRIME TASK FORCE SENT TO MEMPHIS TOPS 10,000 ARRESTS

“We truly feel that Memphis is the model for how you can move forward,” Blackburn said. “Because everyone said we have a problem, here is an opportunity to really surge these resources. Let’s work together and get in behind this and get it done.”

The Memphis Safe Task Force was launched in September 2025, alongside the deployment of the National Guard to the city and increased federal resources to Memphis. Blanche said at Friday’s event that the task force’s work will continue even as they pass the one-year mark. Since the operation began, the Marshals Service has touted more than 13,500 arrests and 2,270 gun seized as part of the crackdown on crime.

articles.headline: Daily on Energy: New England about to be socked with brutal heating oil costs
keyFacts: Heating oil prices rose about 80% over the past year in Maine due to global oil market disruptions, the report stated.
Former regulator Jamie Van Nostrand warned high prices could force families to inadequately heat homes or choose between heating and medical care.
Van Nostrand said high prices will persist through winter and suggested governments provide energy assistance funds to subsidize heating oil.
body: WHAT’S HAPPENING TODAY: Good afternoon and happy Friday, readers! If you don’t have any plans this weekend, the Smithsonian’s National Zoo and Conservation Biology Institute will be hosting their annual “Boo at the Zoo.” It’s an after-hours Halloween event that will feature trick-or-treating stations, a pumpkin patch, and much more. Get tickets here .

Earlier today, Callie spoke with former regulator Jamie Van Nostrand about surging fuel oil prices and how the New England region in particular is feeling the squeeze. Keep reading to see what he suggested as short- and long-term solutions to the growing affordability crisis.

Welcome to Daily on Energy, written by Washington Examiner energy and environment writers Callie Patteson ( @CalliePatteson ) and Maydeen Merino ( @MaydeenMerino ). Email cpatteson@washingtonexaminer dot com or mmerino@washingtonexaminer dot com for tips, suggestions, calendar items, and anything else. If a friend sent this to you and you’d like to sign up, click here . If signing up doesn’t work, shoot us an email, and we’ll add you to our list.
QUOTE OF THE WEEK:
Democrat Sen. John Hickenlooper of Colorado spoke on a podcast this week about the Senate’s plans to take up permitting in November when lawmakers return from midterms.

“I think that it’s going to take a little bit of massaging, because there are some things in there that are going to be tough for some Democrats, and there’s some things in there that are going to be tough for some Republicans. That’s the nature of democracy, right?” Hickenlooper said.

“To get something that matters, both sides have to give a little. So again, I’m not going to prejudge or try to estimate what the votes are going to look like, but I am willing to, and have already made plans to, have a lot of discussions about the bill, so we get a full chance to hear it,” he added.
NEW ENGLAND FEELS THE SQUEEZE FROM OIL:
With snow already falling in northern Maine, homeowners and businesses in New England are preparing to turn on their heat and face record-high heating oil costs.

As we touched on earlier this week , fuel oil costs have surged across the country due to global oil market disruptions caused by a decline in oil flows in the Middle East and loss of refining capacity worldwide. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported in its latest Consumer Price Index that fuel oil prices alone rose by 74.2% for the year ending in September.
Up north, those prices have jumped even higher.
In Maine alone, heating oil prices have risen by around 80% from last year, just below $6 per gallon .
Typically, an oil-heated home can use between 500 and 700 gallons of oil each year. With those prices, families are going to be paying around or more than $4,000 to keep their homes warm this winter.

And in Maine, where around 50% of residents use fuel oil to keep their homes warm, people are going to be feeling “real hardships,” Jamie Van Nostrand , a former regulator in Massachusetts, told Callie today.

Van Nostrand, policy director of the Future of Heat Initiative and former chair of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities, warned that the high prices will stick throughout this winter, which could create dangerous conditions for families.
“It potentially gets to be unsafe because people might not adequately heat their home,” he said.
Additionally, it may cause some homeowners to fall behind in paying their bills, forcing some to choose between things like going to the doctor or heating their home.
“It’s just basic hardship,” he said.

Short-term solutions : The easiest way to address the surging prices locally, Van Nostrand said, is for state officials to offer assistance to homeowners struggling with their bills. The most obvious pathway is through the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program.
Local municipalities have already seen a surge in applications for the assistance, with Aroostook County in Maine alone seeing 16% more this year than in 2025, according to the Bangor Daily News .

Van Nostrand suggested that local governments can go further than that, taking a look at any money that hasn’t been spent and determining if it can be reallocated to subsidize fuel oil over the winter.

There might also be an opportunity for the federal government to take action, with agencies such as the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection Agency issuing emergency orders allowing for additional refining.
A long-term solution: Van Nostrand said higher oil prices present an opportunity for homeowners and businesses to take advantage of alternative heating resources, such as heat pumps.

“The solution to this is going to electric heat pumps, and that’s going to be the lowest cost path,” he said. “And it may be some cold weather states, if you’re already on fuel oil, you could keep that fuel oil as a backup. As it gets below a certain temperature, you go off your electric heat pump and then rely on your fuel oil furnace.”
There is a cost barrier to heat pumps, with whole-home heating systems in cold climates costing around $15,000 to $25,000 to install, Van Nostrand estimates.
However, the Future of Heat initiative has said these systems can save more than $1,000 a year on heating bills, depending on electricity rates.

Van Nostrand noted that as electricity prices increase, the cost of maintaining a heat pump will also rise. But, he insisted that those costs would not be as volatile as just using natural gas to heat your home, as the heat pump draws on a blend of electricity generation.
All the rest:
TRANSMISSION FOR THE VIRGINIAS: The Department of Energy is moving to expand transmission capacity in Virginia and West Virginia, using the Defense Production Act.

The project, announced earlier today, aims to add roughly 290 megawatts of transmission capacity across Appalachian Power’s Virginia grid system, by deploying advanced reconductoring and Dynamic Line Rating technologies. These upgrades are meant to increase the amount of electricity sent to consumers, reduce congestion, and support growing demand.

The project is estimated to take four years, and will be a combined effort by Virginia Energy, Appalachian Power, Potomac Edison, and other regional partners. Through the DPA, the Department of Energy is providing up to $50 million to deploy the transmission upgrades.

Key quote: “A stronger electric grid doesn’t always mean building more power lines. Sometimes it means making better use of the ones we already have,” Office of Electricity Assistant Secretary Katie Jereza said.

As a reminder: In April, President Donald Trump signed five executive orders invoking the DPA, declaring the development, manufacturing, and deployment of large-scale energy infrastructure are critical to national defense. The Cold War-era law gives the president authority to prioritize government funding and contracts for certain industries to support national defense.

OIL BACK ABOVE $100: Domestic oil prices surged back above the $100 line today as Iran escalated its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and the “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine was nowhere in sight.
Just after 3 p.m. EDT, West Texas Intermediate had surged about 3.61% and was selling at $101.51 a barrel. Brent crude also increased 3.60% and was priced at $109.73 a barrel.
“Uncertainty in the Middle East and concerns over the sustainability of oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz has the market pricing in a significant risk premium,” ING analysts said.

LEGISLATION TO BLOCK TRUMP’S RUSSIA DEAL : Prices could see even more upward pressure, as a group of bipartisan lawmakers have introduced a bill that would block Trump’s deal with Russia to supply the world with diesel.
The bill, dubbed the Prohibit Corrupt Russia Oil Deals Act, was introduced today by Democratic Rep. Gregory Meeks , the ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

It would block the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation from investing in Russian energy, nullify general licenses issued by the Treasury permitting the sale of Russian diesel, ban future similar licenses, and mandate the Trump administration to impose sanctions on Russian energy.

“This deal won’t lower costs for the American people, who are already paying for Trump’s failed war of choice in Iran. It will hand Putin millions of dollars to continue slaughtering Ukrainian civilians with impunity,” Meeks said in a statement.
Among the bill’s cosponsors is Rep. Don Bacon , a Republican from Nebraska.

AMERICANS SPENDING MORE ON GAS AND DIESEL: Since March 1st, Americans have now spent $135 billion more on gasoline and diesel purchases compared to the same period last year, Gas Buddy analyst Patrick De Haan said .

The Trump administration has made several efforts to lower prices at the pump for consumers, including making a deal for Russian diesel, pressing Europe to release emergency stock, and temporarily expanding access to dyed diesel.
Yet, prices for diesel remain high.

As of today, the nationwide average price of diesel is at $6.32 per gallon. Diesel prices in several states have increased. For instance, diesel prices in California set an all-time high today of $8.44 per gallon and Colorado hit a new high of $6.48 a gallon.
GLOBAL ELECTRIC VEHICLE SALES FELL 2% IN SEPTEMBER: Global sales for electric vehicles declined by 2% in September, breaking a six-month upward trend.

The Benchmark Mineral Intelligence said in a report that 2.15 million electric vehicles were sold globally in September, bringing this year’s EV sales to 15.5 million. EV sales month-on-month did rise 17%, but were down 2% year-on-year.
Benchmark Mineral Intelligence Data Manager Charles Lester said the decline is partially driven by a weaker North American market and a slowdown in China.

However, Europe had its strongest month on record, selling almost 600,000 EVs last month, which is about 10% more than the previous high set in June. Sales in Europe were up 39% year-on-year. The United Kingdom, France, Spain, Portugal, and Finland had record-high monthly EV sales.
Meanwhile, North America sales fell 44% year-on-year, which is the steepest decline of the year.
FRANCE AND GERMANY PUSH TO END 2035 CLIMATE GOALS FOR CARS: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expects the European Union to water down emissions rules for new fuel-burning cars.

Bloomberg reports that Germany and France have joined forces to try to end the EU’s goal of reaching climate neutrality for cars by 2035 as part of an effort to protect domestic industries. Some of the biggest carmakers are in Germany and France.
“We reached an agreement between Germany and France on future policy toward the automotive industry,” Merz told reporters in Brussels. “With this, the combustion engine ban is history.”
Germany and France will lobby to weaken a key pillar in the EU’s green deal, which seeks to reach net-zero by 2050.
The two countries are seeking to lower overall emissions cuts for autos to 90% by 2035, without having to compensate the remaining 10% through offsets via renewable fuels and green steel.

articles.headline: Five of the web's biggest data-scraping brands now sit under one $3.6 billion umbrella, and AI agents are the reason why
keyFacts: Five web-scraping brands, including Oxylabs and Decodo, have formally united under a Vilnius-based umbrella organization named Source.
Source claims demand across its companies grew fourfold in a year as artificial intelligence agents pulled live web data.
Source is expanding into dedicated web search APIs built specifically for artificial intelligence agents.
body: - Oxylabs, Decodo, Webshare, ScrapingBee, and Honeygain now formally sit under one Vilnius-based umbrella called Source
- Source claims AI agents drove a fourfold increase in demand for services across its organizations
- The brands, previously reviewed as rivals, including three of TechRadar's nine best-proxy picks, now officially share common oversight
Oxylabs, Decodo, Webshare, ScrapingBee, and Honeygain have formally come together under a single name, Source, and the Lithuanian group behind them says AI agents are why it needed one.
The Vilnius-based ecosystem claims demand across its companies has risen fourfold in a year as AI agents, next-generation search tools, and frontier AI products pull live data from the web.
Its systems now process 1.5 million requests per second, and that it is expanding into web search APIs built specifically for AI agents.
One umbrella with five different, competing shopfronts?

Source presents itself as a backbone rather than a business. Its launch post says it has no customers or products of its own; instead, it handles patents, procurement, hiring, and compliance, while each brand keeps its own team, product strategy, and customer base.

The brands are split by customer type. Oxylabs serves enterprises and AI labs; Decodo (formerly Smartproxy) targets the mid-market; ScrapingBee sells developer APIs; Webshare serves professional consumers and solo builders; and Honeygain pays ordinary people for their spare bandwidth.

For anyone shopping for a proxy service, this is the most practical takeaway. Oxylabs bought Webshare in 2022 and ScrapingBee in 2025, and Honeygain became its main residential proxy sourcing partner in 2021.

Decodo's ties were less clear-cut until now, and trade site Proxyway notes that the launch officially links Oxylabs and Decodo under one organization. Source CEO Vytautas Savickas ran Decodo until March 2026, when he moved across to lead the Oxylabs group and founder Julius Černiauskas became chairman.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!

All of this points to a marriage of convenience rather than a merger by organizations that are already very closely interlinked. This is interesting because some of these brands have been sold and reviewed as alternatives to one another.

The best example of this is that three of the nine picks in TechRadar's own best proxy sites guide now belong to Source: Decodo as best overall, Oxylabs as best for business, and Webshare as best for privacy.

For context on the overlap, our residential proxy roundup described Oxylabs as one of Decodo's toughest competitors. Source says the companies remain fully independent in strategy, customers, and market presence, and that may well hold commercially, but common oversight is now a matter of record.
The release provided to TechRadar says Source gives the group "a unified voice in defending responsible access to public web data," and its legal history explains the appetite.

Reddit sued Oxylabs alongside Perplexity, SerpApi and AWMProxy in October 2025, alleging they evaded its anti-scraping measures by lifting Reddit content from Google search results. Oxylabs said it was "shocked and disappointed" and would defend itself.

It was still listed as a defendant in filings this spring, and in late July a federal judge allowed Reddit's core claims against SerpApi and Perplexity to proceed. Further back, a Texas jury awarded rival Bright Data nearly $7.5 million against Oxylabs in a 2021 patent case.

Source's own essay on AI agents and the open web argues that if access is negotiated one licensing deal at a time, only the biggest companies will be able to afford it. This makes a convenient argument for a large web scraping group, but the gatekeeping fears are real.

The most concrete product promised here is AI search, and it is older than the umbrella itself: Oxylabs already offers a Web API that pairs a search endpoint with a scraping endpoint for agents, so the "dedicated AI Search APIs" promised look more like an expansion of existing work than a new product line.
For customers, the questions to watch are whether the brands keep competing on price, how clearly each one discloses their newfound relationship, and how the Reddit case plays out for Oxylabs.

For everyone else, Source is a bet that AI agents will keep needing the live web, and that the companies supplying the pipes deserve a seat at the table when the rules for that access get written, aiming to negotiate from a clustered position of strength.

articles.headline: ‘I served with Ilhan Omar’s father in the Somali military — people were scared of him’: ex-officer
keyFacts: A retired Somali officer told The Post that Representative Ilhan Omar's late father was a colonel in dictator Siad Barre's regime.
Omar's father allegedly concealed his military past when seeking United States asylum, which could affect the status of his children.
Sources familiar with the investigation said the Trump administration is building a case that could lead to Representative Omar's deportation.
body: Rep. Ilhan Omar’s father was a “feared” colonel in the Somali National Army (SNA), far from the “educator” he was presented to Americans as, a veteran who served in his regiment claimed to The Post.

Nur Omar Mohamed has been accused of hiding his military past from US authorities when he arrived and claimed asylum with his family in 1995 — which could have disqualified him from claiming refugee status.
A retired military officer still living in Somalia has spoken out for the first time to shed light on the “career soldier” who was a trusted operator in dictator Siad Barre’s brutal regime.
“I used to serve in the military with Nur, he was the colonel of my regiment and I would see him face-to-face,” the veteran, who wished to remain anonymous for fear of reprisals, told The Post.
“He was a full, top colonel. And no one gets to that position by being a nice guy. He was obviously good at what he did.
“I remember him always dressed in a smart military uniform with his rifle hanging off a strap behind him. Some people were scared of him and would look away when he walked past.”
The former soldier is confused as to why Omar, 44, portrayed her father, who died in 2020, as a teacher in her 2020 memoir “My Journey from Refugee to Congresswoman.”

“Nur was very recognizable at the military hub in the city of Baidoa. He was one of those picked to be trained in Egypt in the 60s. He rose very quickly to the top of the military and became a trusted man [in the regime].”
Nur went on to play an “important part” in the Somali-Ethiopian war between July 1977 and March 1978, the former army officer claimed.
“He worked with the masterminds of the invasion and was trusted with the plans, he helped organize the troops. But a lot of people died in that war,” he told The Post.
If it emerges Nur lied on US immigration forms, it could have implications for his children who emigrated with him.
Omar has denied she ever committed any kind of immigration fraud. Her representatives declined to comment to The Post.
Omar’s father, who died from COVID-19 complications aged 67, is said to have joined the SNA in the late ‘60s and specialized in air defense before moving into the infantry.
He allegedly played a key role in Barre’s army after the bloodthirsty dictator seized power in a Soviet-backed coup in 1969.
Nur, born in the Somali coastal town of Bandarbeyla, part of the semi-autonomous region of Puntland, climbed up the military ranks to colonel.
But his “prestigious” military career came to an end when Barre was ousted in 1991 after two decades of oppression that saw up to 200,000 civilians killed and millions displaced.

Although there is no evidence of Nur committing war crimes, expert historian Mohamed Haji Ingiriis has accused him of being complicit in Barre’s regime and said that he “assisted the dictator to remain in power for so long”.
Nur went with his family to a refugee camp in Kenya before arriving in the US as refugees, settling in Minneapolis. Nur worked as a taxi driver and postal worker to make ends meet.
However, sources told The Post that for years after arriving in America, he was still involved in local politics in Puntland and was advising the troops in clan wars.
“He was a real military man, it was his whole life,” the veteran in Somalia added.

body: A Biden-appointed judge dismissed former CIA Director John Brennan's lawsuit against President Donald Trump and senior administration officials, ruling that his concerns about the potential destruction of evidence needed for a future criminal defense were too "speculative."

The dismissal comes as Brennan faces two federal investigations, including a Justice Department probe into whether former intelligence officials conspired to violate Trump's civil rights through investigations into alleged ties between his 2016 presidential campaign and Russia.

A separate investigation is examining whether Brennan made false statements during 2023 congressional testimony about the Steele dossier's role in a 2017 intelligence assessment of Russian interference in the presidential election.
FORMER CIA DIRECTOR BRENNAN SUBPOENAED TO TESTIFY IN FEDERAL TRUMP CONSPIRACY CASE

Trump has repeatedly accused Brennan, President Barack Obama and other former intelligence officials of orchestrating the "Russia collusion hoax," but they have rejected those accusations, claiming that the administration is attempting to discredit legitimate intelligence findings about Russian interference in the 2016 election.

While Judge Jia Cobb called Brennan’s allegations that the Trump administration was targeting him for opposing the president "deeply concerning," she ruled that he lacked standing to sue because he had not shown that officials were likely destroying records relevant to a potential defense, and the injury he feared depended on a series of events that had not yet occurred.

"For Brennan’s constitutional injury to actually accrue, a series of dominoes must fall, and Defendants’ deletion of records is just one of those dominoes," Cobb wrote. "There is no dispute about this: Defendants describe this domino chain in their motion to dismiss...and Brennan accepts it in his response."

Brennan has been identified as a target in two federal investigations that have involved three grand jury inquiries — two in the Southern District of Florida and one in Washington, D.C. — but he has not been charged with a crime. The former CIA director was subpoenaed to testify before a federal grand jury in Fort Pierce, Florida, on Oct. 15, though his scheduled appearance was postponed.

Brennan filed his lawsuit naming Trump, FBI Director Kash Patel, Attorney General Todd Blanche, CIA Director John Ratcliffe, and other officials on July 1, 2026. The 46-page lawsuit , accused the Justice Department of handling its investigation into Brennan with "unprecedented, irregular conduct" that was driven by the "president’s retribution agenda."
DELETED EMAIL DETAILS ALLEGED TRUMP-TARGETING PUSH INSIDE LETITIA JAMES’ OFFICE: ‘FIND AND PURSUE CRIMES’

Brennan argued that key evidence could disappear before he had a chance to challenge any future indictment. He pointed to deleted social-media posts, the administration’s use of Signal and other messaging tools with auto-delete features, unpreserved texts and direct messages, AI queries, Microsoft Teams chats, and alleged failures to preserve discovery in other cases, including the prosecution of Rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J. He said the loss of those records could make it harder to determine whether the investigations were based on legitimate law enforcement concerns or political retaliation.

"With this lawsuit, Director Brennan has served notice that the government’s conduct and its document preservation will be carefully scrutinized in the event of any future indictment. Director Brennan will continue to vigorously defend himself against these baseless investigations, and he will challenge any attempt to use the criminal justice system for personal and political retribution," Brennan’s lawyers, Ken Wainstein and Dan Gelber told the AP.
The lawsuit also pointed to what it described as irregularities in the Justice Department’s handling of the investigation.

It cited the removal of longtime DOJ prosecutor Maria Medetis Long, who was reportedly taken off the Brennan investigation in April 2026 after expressing doubts about the strength of the case, as evidence of what it described as irregular conduct. She was replaced by Trump ally Joseph diGenova, who later resigned from his role overseeing the investigation amid reported internal disagreements over the handling of the case.
TRUMP SAYS HE WILL NOMINATE ACTING AG TODD BLANCHE TO PERMANENTLY LEAD JUSTICE DEPARTMENT

Brennan’s attorneys accused the Justice Department of "judge-shopping" by trying to steer grand jury proceedings toward Trump-appointed Judge Aileen Cannon in Fort Pierce, Florida, rather than allowing the case to proceed through the court's normal assignment process. They also questioned why prosecutors were pursuing the investigation in Florida when much of the allegations occurred in Washington, D.C.

The complaint also accused DOJ and FBI leaders of improperly discussing details of the investigations publicly, raising questions about whether officials disclosed information that should have remained confidential.It cited Attorney General Todd Blanche’s statements that DOJ had issued "200 grand jury subpoenas" and was investigating a "pattern of behavior" to "destroy" Trump, as well as FBI Director Kash Patel’s public discussion of the investigations and their targets.
Fox News Digital reached out to the Justice Department for comment.

articles.headline: White House Press Secretary Zacharia exiting role after short tenure
keyFacts: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is leaving her position after five days, according to US news outlets.
President Donald Trump said he advised Zacharia to reconsider her role following her brief first press briefing.
Zacharia faced controversy because neither she nor the White House provided evidence that she was licensed to practice law.
body: New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is on the way out from her position, the New York Times and other US news outlets reported on Friday.

Zacharia started her new job just five days ago, taking over for Karoline Leavitt. She had a nervy first White House briefing with journalists on Tuesday, fielding just three questions and leaving the podium after a little under 14 minutes.

Earlier on Friday, President Donald Trump suggested that Zacharia might be leaving. "I told her: 'I think you're better off being happy, and I'm not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.' There's nothing easy about this stuff," Trump told reporters.
He added: "I said to her honestly, 'If I were you, I'd reconsider... think about it. But I would reconsider.'"
Last Friday, Trump announced Zacharia's appointment as the new press secretary. However, she became embroiled in controversy when her previous claims to be a lawyer were revealed to be false.
Controversy swirled around Zacharia's legal background
Until last week, Zacharia was a commentator for conservative outlets Fox News and Newsmax. She also advised the Trump Media and Technology, the company behind Trump's Truth Social platform.

Zacharia has also long described herself as a lawyer, but her credentials remain unverified. Neither she nor the White House has provided evidence that she passed the bar exam in any state or in China, where she worked for a large law firm years ago.

According to her LinkedIn profile, Zacharia was an associate at Zhong Lun Law Firm in Beijing from 2011 to 2013. She was also a general counsel at Fix California, an advocacy group founded by Trump ally Ric Grenell, from 2024 to 2025.

Zacharia earned her law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011. While nearly all licensed US lawyers first obtain a law degree, law school graduates cannot legally practice law in the US without first being admitted to a state bar.
